title: LLM experiment traffic conductivity notes (working)
content:
Purpose:
To codify heuristics and quick experiments for detecting and mitigating cross-cohort contamination during staggered LLM rollouts. Working metaphors: traffic conductivity (how easily signals migrate between slices), bleed, and nodes (entry points like API routes, SDK clients, internal batch jobs).

TL;DR (notes to self):
- Focus instrumentation on session/user-level continuity (session_id, user_id, route) to compute conductivity scores.
- Synthetic microtraffic can validate isolation; run 3 gradients: isolated, low-leak, deliberate-leak.
- If conductivity > threshold, quarantine slice and run rollback within 5m.

Definitions (informal):
- Conductivity: fraction of requests from slice A that end up referencing or being influenced by outputs previously served by slice B within X minutes. (proxy for contamination)
- Bleed: observable behavioral drift in metric distributions attributable to cross-slice interactions.
- Echo: identical or near-identical outputs repeated across sessions that indicate caching/routing artifacts.

Measurement plan (what to capture):
1) session_id, user_tier, client_version, assigned_slice, route, request_sha, prompt_signature, model_variant, response_hash, kv_cache_hit (bool), timestamp
2) compute per-slice conductivity = (#responses in slice A that include response_hash previously emitted by slice B within 10m) / total_responses_A
3) compute drift-adjusted latency/cost deltas and normalize by traffic volume

Quick SQL snippets (pseudocode):
- recent_hashes = select distinct response_hash, assigned_slice from responses where timestamp > now() - interval '10 minutes';
- conductivity = select a.assigned_slice as target_slice, b.assigned_slice as source_slice, count(*) / total_target as conductivity_score from responses a join recent_hashes b on a.response_hash = b.response_hash and a.assigned_slice != b.assigned_slice group by target_slice, source_slice;

Heuristics and gates (first pass):
- soft-watch: conductivity > 0.005 -> notify steward, increase sampling of human-review prompts for that cohort
- hard-quarantine: conductivity > 0.02 OR simultaneous latency regressions >20% across >3 slices -> remove exposure and re-evaluate rollout config
- isolation sanity-check: run synthetic isolated traffic for 30m after any deployment change; expected conductivity < 0.0005

Traffic shaping patterns we want to test (experiments):
- serpentine allocation: interleaved micro-batches across time windows to reduce burst-induced routing collisions
- cohort moat: pin new model to unique client_version and route variant for first 48h to reduce interop leakage
- KV-segmentation: prefer per-slice KV namespaces in serving runtime to reduce cached cross-pollination

Operational playbook (short):
- Pre-rollout: add extra response_hash sampling (1/10 of requests) + enable extended trace logs in canary nodes
- During rollout: steward watches conductivity dashboard (rolling 10m, 1h) + daily owner sync if traffic >5k/min
- Post-detect: temp roll forward to narrower cohort (micro-quarantine), trigger replay of synthetic traffic to validate fix, then resume slow ramp

Open questions / TODOs:
- What is a defensible window for counting contamination (10m above is guessy). Need historical replay experiments to tune.
- How to treat cross-device identical responses from deterministic models vs harmful contamination? Need fingerprint heuristics that consider similarity not just exact hash.
- Integrate with Optimize recommendations: can we suggest KV namespace assignment automatically? (linked PR above)

Risks & tradeoffs:
- Aggressive quarantining reduces rollout speed and hurts PLG experience. Need to parameterize steward alert severity by customer tier.
- Synthetic traffic can be costly but catches subtle leaks earlier — budget for small but targeted sim clusters.

Quick checklist for an experiment run (commander one-pager):
- [ ] Register experiment in JIRA and link to this doc (JIRA-PLAT-789)
- [ ] Create cohort with dedicated KV namespace and client tag
- [ ] Enable response_hash sampling and 10m conductivity metric
- [ ] Run synthetic isolated baseline for 30m and record conductivity
- [ ] Ramp 0.5% -> 2% -> 10% with 30–60m holds, monitor conductivity/latency/cost
- [ ] If conductivity breach -> trigger micro-quarantine and notify on-call

Notes / field observations from quick lab:
- In yesterday's lab, a single shared caching layer caused 0.012 conductivity between two variants after 45m — fixed by namespace split (immediate drop to ~0.0003).
- SDK older than v1.3.2 sometimes reuses connections in ways that route cached prefix tokens; recommended pin for new cohort.

Reference links & artifacts:
- rollout sim repo PR: github.com/redwood-inference/rollout-sim/pull/42
- short deck for legal: CONF-1234
- ticket for telemetry infra: JIRA-PLAT-789

Notes to self: keep this doc light and experimental. If we get 1–2 more real-case blips, formalize into a runbook with dashboard widgets and automated quarantine remediations.

---
End of working notes.
